name: Team 4   /   Project presentation
text: Team 4   /   Project presentation

Suggested time: 20 seconds.
Finora is our personal finance project. It helps people understand the money they earn, the money they spend, and what remains at the end of the month. Today we will show the experience through a simple example.
Project sources: finora-template/README.md, finora-template/src/App.tsx, finora-template/src/data.ts. Original brand artwork: finora-template/public/finora-icon.svg and finora-wordmark.svg.
Presentation references: https://www.monarch.com/ and https://www.ynab.com/ (accessed 12 October 2026). These informed the plain-language, benefit-first product narrative. No competitor statistics or features are attributed to Finora.

Suggested time: 30 seconds.
Think about payday. Money arrives, then rent, groceries and smaller purchases follow. Looking only at a balance does not tell us which categories used the money or whether we are close to a limit. This is the everyday problem our project addresses. These are problem scenarios, not research statistics.
Source: README.md project problem statement.

Here is the starting point in the Finora template. Income is 5,250 dollars, expenses are 2,864 dollars, and the difference is 2,386 dollars. Finora calls that monthly savings. This is a calculated difference in recorded transactions, not a claim about a separate bank savings account.

A user adds an income or expense entry with an amount, date and category. The transaction list keeps those entries together, and the filters help find a particular month or kind of spending. Users can edit mistakes or remove an entry. For a live demonstration, add a small food expense and then filter to Food.

Suggested time: 40 seconds.
Users choose a monthly budget for a category. Finora compares recorded spending with that limit. In the template, under 80 percent is on track, 80 to 100 percent is near the limit, and more than 100 percent is exceeded. Here entertainment spending is 225 dollars against a 200-dollar limit, so the warning explains that it is 25 dollars over. This gives a concrete reason to review the next purchase.

Suggested time: 35 seconds.
The monthly report puts the spending categories in context. In this sample month, housing is the largest category at 1,400 dollars, or 48.9 percent of total spending. That is a description of the example, not advice to change a particular expense. The template also offers Excel export so users can keep a copy of the report.

Suggested time: 20 seconds, then demo or questions.
Our goal is to make everyday finances easier to understand. The short demo follows one expense: add it to Transactions, check its category budget, then open the Monthly Report.
If asked about readiness: the repository documents connected transactions, budgets and monthly reports with a NestJS backend. Dashboard and Income pages are still in progress. The backend keeps changes through browser refreshes but resets when the server restarts. The standalone template resets on browser reload and has no bank connection or authentication.
Sources: finora/client/README.md, api/README.md and finora-template/README.md.
